:::{.def}

For this course, we have already installed the required packages, but this section is important for you when you want to install packages on your machine or on the Alliance clusters.

:::

## On your machine

:::{.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="default"}

## Supported platforms for JAX

Before you install the stack, you need to check whether your machine is able to run JAX on GPU (all systems can run JAX on CPU).

|            | Linux x86_64 | Linux aarch64 | Mac aarch64  | Windows x86_64 | Windows WSL2 x86_64 |
|------------|--------------|---------------|--------------|----------------|---------------------|
| CPU        | yes          | yes           | yes          | yes            | yes                 |
| NVIDIA GPU | yes          | yes           | n/a          | no             | experimental        |
| Google TPU | yes          | n/a           | n/a          | n/a            | n/a                 |
| AMD GPU    | yes          | no            | n/a          | no             | experimental        |
| Apple GPU  | n/a          | no            | experimental | n/a            | n/a                 |
| Intel GPU  | experimental | n/a           | n/a          | no             | no                  |

[from the [JAX documentation](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/installation.html#supported-platforms)]{.caption}

:::

On your machine ([but not on the Alliance clusters](https://docs.alliancecan.ca/wiki/Uv)), I recommend that you use [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) to create a Python project with your chosen Python version and all the necessary packages. `uv` installs packages much faster than `pip` and it is able to resolve dependencies very well. It also manages Python versions.

:::{.note}

If you want more information on this, I gave [a webinar on `uv`](/python/wb_uv) in May 2025.

:::

Create a Python project (let's call it `jaxai`) and `cd` into it:

```{.bash}
uv init --bare jaxai
cd jaxai
```

:::{.note}

`--bare` creates a `uv` project without files that I am not interested in here such as a [README]{.codelike} and a [main.py]{.codelike}.

:::

Install the packages:

```{.bash}
uv add dm-pix imageio jax-ai-stack "jax[cuda13]" matplotlib orbax polars scikit-image tqdm "transformers==4.57.3"
```

:::{.note}

Quick explanation of packages we are installing:

```
- dm-pix                ➔ for data augmentation
- imageio               ➔ to load images into NumPy arrays
- jax-ai-stack          ➔ installs JAX for the CPU (if not already installed for the GPU),
                                   Flax—the main NN library,
                                   Optax—optimizers & loss functions,
                                   Orbax—for checkpointing,
                                   Grain—to build efficient dataloaders,
          						   ml_dtypes—NumPy dtype extensions for deep learning
- jax[cuda13]           ➔ only if you want to run JAX on GPUs (use an appropriate version of Cuda)
- matplotlib            ➔ to display samples
- orbax                 ➔ checkpointing and saving model
- polars                ➔ for DataFrames
- scikit-image          ➔ image resizing
- tqdm                  ➔ display progress bars
- transformers          ➔ load model and pre-trained weights from Hugging Face model Hub
                          We pin the version because v5 will not support JAX anymore
```

If you install packages which depend on JAX (e.g. Flax), they will by default install the CPU version of JAX. If you want to run JAX on GPUs, make sure to install `jax[cuda13]` (or whatever Cuda version is suitable).

:::

You will see that the dependencies have automatically populated a `pyproject.toml` file and that a virtual environment called `.venv` was created.

As long as you are within the project, you don't need to activate that virtual environment: all you need to do is run `python`/`jupyter lab`/`ipython`/`ptpython`/a `.py` script after `uv run`.

:::{.example}

Examples:

```{.bash}
$ uv run python
$ uv run jupyter lab
$ uv run ptpython
$ uv run my_script.py
```

:::

You can even launch Jupyter lab within a project without installing it in that project by using:

```{.bash}
$ uv run --with jupyter jupyter lab
```

Alternatively, if you really want a `pip` equivalent (for backward compatibility with old pipelines for instance), you can activate it as you would any other Python virtual environment:

```{.bash}
source .venv/bin/activate
```

### Sharing uv projects

To share your uv project environment (for instance for collaboration), put the [pyproject.toml]{.codelike} and [uv.lock]{.codelike} files under version control (or distribute them to your collaborators by other means): they pin every version of Python and the installed packages.

A collaborator can recreate the environment (install the proper Python version if missing and install all packages at the pinned versions) by cd-ing into the project and running:

```{.bash}
$ uv sync
```

## On an Alliance cluster

:::{.note}

I already installed all the necessary packages in the training cluster to save time and space. The instructions for today thus differ from what you would normally do and production cluster instructions in the second tab are for your future reference only.

:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Today

Look for available Python modules:

```{.bash}
module spider python
```

Load version 3.11.5:

```{.bash}
module load python/3.11.5
```

I created a virtual Python environment with all necessary packages under `/project`. All you have to do today is activate it with:

```{.bash}
source /project/def-sponsor00/nabirds_venv/bin/activate
```

### Production cluster

Look for available Python modules:

```{.bash}
module spider python
```

Load the version of your choice:

```{.bash}
module load python/3.13.2
```

Create a Python virtual environment:

```{.bash}
python -m venv ~/env
```

Activate it:

```{.bash}
source ~/env/bin/activate
```

Update pip from wheel:

```{.bash}
python -m pip install --upgrade --no-index pip
```

:::{.notenoit}

Whenever a [Python wheel](https://pythonwheels.com/) for a package is available on the Alliance clusters, you should use it instead of downloading the package from [PyPI](https://pypi.org/). To do this, simply add the `--no-index` flag to the install command.

You can see whether a wheel is available with `avail_wheels <package>` or look at [the list of available wheels](https://docs.alliancecan.ca/wiki/Available_Python_wheels).

Advantages of wheels:

- compiled for the clusters' hardware,
- ensures no missing or conflicting dependencies,
- much faster installation.

:::

Install libraries from wheel:

```{.bash}
python -m pip install --no-index dm-pix imageio jax-ai-stack "jax[cuda]" matplotlib orbax polars scikit-image tqdm "transformers==4.57.1"
```

:::{.notenoit}

- Don't forget `--no-index` to install from wheels.

- On the cluster, we pin the `transformers` version to `4.57.1` because this is the highest v4 present.

:::

:::{.info}

We don't have `cuda13` on the Alliance clusters yet. If you follow [JAX official installation instructions](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/installation.html) and try to install `jax[cuda13]`, `pip` will default to installing `jax` (CPU only).

Make sure to use `jax[cuda]` (or the equivalent `jax[cuda12]`) instead to have the GPU version installed.

:::

:::

## Moving from your computer to the cluster

If you prototyped your project locally and want to move it to an Alliance cluster to run it at scale, here are some tips.

### Environment

Install the packages in a Python virtual environment with `venv` and `pip` as shown above.

### Code

Clone the project from a Git remote (or [copy it with `scp -r` or `rsync`](../../bash/intro_transfer.qmd)):

```{.bash}
[local]$ scp -r </path/to/local/project> <user>@<cluster>.alliancecan.ca:~/<path/to/remote/project>
```

### Data

Deep learning datasets often contain many small files (e.g. images), but clusters are slowed to a crawl by swarms of small files.

Pack the data directory into an archive on your machine and copy the archive to the cluster:

```{.bash}
[local]$ tar cf data.tar -C </path/to/local/project/data>
[local]$ scp data.tar <user>@<cluster>.alliancecan.ca:~/projects/def-<user>/
```

:::{.note}

If the archive is very large, you can use [Globus](../jxai/jxai_getdata.qmd#globus) for the transfer.

:::

Then keep the archive as is on the cluster and only extract it *inside jobs*.
